## Streaming implementation — core layer

**`src/core/streaming.ts`** — the foundational SSE stream implementation.
- `class Stream<Item>` implements `AsyncIterable<Item>`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, controller, client?, synthesizeEventData?)` — parses a `fetch` `Response` into an async-iterable stream of JSON events by consuming SSE frames.
- `_iterSSEMessages()` / `iterSSEChunks()` / `class SSEDecoder` — low-level SSE frame/line decoding (uses `src/internal/decoders/line.ts`'s `LineDecoder`).
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — alternate constructor for newline-delimited JSON streams (used by the `lib/*Stream` helpers' `fromReadableStream` methods, e.g. for replaying a previously-saved stream).
- `Stream.tee()` — splits a stream for independent consumption.

`src/streaming.ts` is just a deprecated re-export of `./core/streaming`.

**`src/internal/parse.ts`** (`defaultParseResponse`) is where the dispatch happens: if `props.options.stream` is true, it calls `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (or `Stream.fromSSEResponse` by default). This is invoked from the low-level HTTP client in **`src/client.ts`**, so every resource method that passes `stream: true` in its request options gets routed through here automatically.

## Higher-level streaming helpers (`src/lib/`)

Built on top of `core/streaming.ts`, these add event-emitter ergonomics, accumulation into a final object, and (for chat) tool-calling loops:
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — base class (`EventStream<EventTypes>`) with `.on()`, `.emit()`, abort handling.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `class ChatCompletionStream` extends `AbstractChatCompletionRunner`; static `createChatCompletion(client, params, options)` and `fromReadableStream()`.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` / `AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts` — tool-calling runner variant used by `runTools()` when `stream: true`.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `class ResponseStream extends EventStream<ResponseEvents>`; static `createResponse(client, params, options)`.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `class AssistantStream extends EventStream<AssistantStreamEvents>`; static `createAssistantStream(...)` and `fromReadableStream()` (Assistants/beta API).
- `src/realtime/*` (`OpenAIRealtimeEmitter`, `OpenAIRealtimeWebSocket`, `OpenAIRealtimeWS`) — a **separate**, WebSocket-based (not SSE) streaming mechanism for the Realtime API; does not go through `core/streaming.ts`.

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Resource method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` / `.retrieve({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-168` | returns `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` via `_client.post`/`get` with `stream: body.stream` |
| `client.responses.stream(body)` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:201-206` | calls `ResponseStream.createResponse()` |
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:63-79` | `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(body)` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:221-226` | calls `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion()` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(body)` with `stream:true` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:195-212` | delegates to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools()` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy Completions API) | `src/resources/completions.ts:28-43` | `APIPromise<Stream<Completion>>` |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` / `.generate({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:45-91` | `APIPromise<Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent \| ImageGenStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:31-63` | `APIPromise<Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream:true})` / `.submitToolOutputs({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:57-263` (deprecated Assistants API) | `APIPromise<Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / `.createAndStream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:165-234` | calls `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream()` |
| Realtime API (`client.realtime`, `beta/realtime`) | `src/realtime/websocket.ts`, `src/realtime/ws.ts` | separate WebSocket-based streaming, not SSE |

All the "`create*({stream:true})`" entries share one pattern verified directly: they pass `stream: body.stream ?? false` into `this._client.post/get(...)`, and the client's shared response parser (`src/internal/parse.ts:24-40`) is what actually calls `Stream.fromSSEResponse` (or a custom `__streamClass`) when `options.stream` is true — this is the single chokepoint all SSE-based streaming methods funnel through.

**Not verified:** I didn't read `lib/ChatCompletionRunner.ts`, `lib/RunnableFunction.ts`, `lib/responses/ResponseAccumulator.ts`, or the realtime `sessions.ts`/`transcription-sessions.ts` bodies in detail, nor did I execute/test any of this code — this is a static-read analysis via `ghx` only, no clone.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

# OpenAI TypeScript and JavaScript API Library

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```
